name: Veg Hakka Noodles

ingredients.name: Salt (for the boiling water)
ingredients.householdMeasure: ½ tsp (most of it is drained away)

ingredients.name: Vegetable oil (groundnut/sunflower/rice bran)
ingredients.householdMeasure: 2½ tsp (½ tsp to toss the boiled noodles, 2 tsp to stir-fry)

ingredients.name: Spring onion (hara pyaz)
ingredients.householdMeasure: 2 stalks; whites chopped separately from the greens

ingredients.name: Carrot (gajar)
ingredients.householdMeasure: ¼ medium carrot, cut into thin matchsticks

ingredients.name: Green capsicum (shimla mirch)
ingredients.householdMeasure: ¼ medium capsicum, cut into thin strips

ingredients.name: French beans
ingredients.householdMeasure: 4–5 beans, sliced thinly on a slant

ingredients.name: Black pepper powder (kali mirch) (or white pepper)
Salt (for the stir-fry)
ingredients.householdMeasure: 1 small pinch (taste first; soy sauce is salty)

equipment: Large pot or deep pan for boiling the noodles (at least 2 litres)
Tongs or two forks for tossing the noodles
Chopping board and a sharp knife
A plate or tray to spread the drained noodles on
Small bowls to keep each vegetable ready

steps.title: Pour 1.5 litres (about 6 cups) water into the large pot, add ½ tsp salt, and put it on high heat
steps.text: Pour 1.5 litres (about 6 cups) water into the large pot, add ½ tsp salt, and put it on high heat
steps.tip: lots of water stops the noodles sticking. Chop the vegetables while it heats.
steps.visualCue: pot on the flame, lid on to boil faster
steps.cameraCheck: the pot of water on the stove
steps.videoShot: water poured into a pot and salt sprinkled in

steps.title: Peel and finely chop 3 garlic cloves (6 g)
steps.text: Peel and finely chop 3 garlic cloves (6 g)
steps.visualCue: tiny pieces about the size of a sesame seed
steps.cameraCheck: the chopped garlic on the board
steps.videoShot: knife rocking over the garlic

steps.title: Peel and finely chop ½ inch ginger (3 g), and slit or chop 1 green chilli if using
steps.text: Peel and finely chop ½ inch ginger (3 g), and slit or chop 1 green chilli if using
steps.visualCue: two small piles of fine pieces
steps.videoShot: ginger sliced into thin strips, then chopped

steps.title: Thinly slice ¼ medium onion (30 g) lengthwise
steps.text: Thinly slice ¼ medium onion (30 g) lengthwise
steps.visualCue: thin half-moon slivers that separate into strands
steps.videoShot: onion sliced from root to tip

steps.title: Chop 2 spring onion stalks, keeping the white part and the green part in separate piles

steps.visualCue: a small pile of white rings and a larger pile of green pieces
steps.cameraCheck: the two piles side by side
steps.videoShot: knife slicing across the stalks

steps.title: Finely shred ¾ cup cabbage (40 g)
steps.text: Finely shred ¾ cup cabbage (40 g)
steps.visualCue: long thin pale-green strands, similar in thickness to the noodles
steps.videoShot: knife shredding a cabbage wedge

steps.title: Peel ¼ carrot (30 g) and cut it into thin matchsticks
steps.text: Peel ¼ carrot (30 g) and cut it into thin matchsticks
steps.tip: long thin strips mix with the noodles better than cubes and cook in the same time.
steps.visualCue: thin orange sticks about 4–5 cm long
steps.videoShot: carrot sliced into thin planks, then into sticks

steps.title: Deseed ¼ capsicum (30 g) and cut it into thin strips
steps.text: Deseed ¼ capsicum (30 g) and cut it into thin strips
steps.visualCue: thin green strips
steps.videoShot: capsicum cut into long strips

steps.title: Trim 4–5 French beans (20 g) and slice them thinly on a slant
steps.text: Trim 4–5 French beans (20 g) and slice them thinly on a slant
steps.visualCue: thin, long diagonal green slices
steps.videoShot: beans sliced at an angle

steps.title: Mix 2 tsp soy sauce, 1 tsp vinegar and 1 tsp green chilli sauce in a small cup, and keep ¼ tsp pepper, a pinch of salt and a pinch of sugar beside it
steps.text: Mix 2 tsp soy sauce, 1 tsp vinegar and 1 tsp green chilli sauce in a small cup, and keep ¼ tsp pepper, a pinch of salt and a pinch of sugar beside it
steps.tip: line everything up next to the stove in the order you will use it. The stir-fry takes only 5 minutes.
steps.visualCue: a small cup of dark-brown sauce next to the dry seasonings
steps.videoShot: soy sauce and vinegar poured into a cup and stirred

steps.title: When the water is at a full rolling boil, add 75 g dry noodles (half a packet)
steps.text: When the water is at a full rolling boil, add 75 g dry noodles (half a packet)
steps.visualCue: big bubbles all over the surface before the noodles go in
steps.cameraCheck: the noodles going into the boiling water
steps.videoShot: a noodle brick lowered into bubbling water

steps.title: Boil the noodles, loosening them gently with tongs or a fork after the first minute
steps.text: Boil the noodles, loosening them gently with tongs or a fork after the first minute
steps.tip: overcooked noodles turn mushy and break in the wok. They cook a little more during the stir-fry.
steps.visualCue: the noodles are soft and flexible but a broken strand still has a tiny firm white dot in the centre (al dente)
steps.cameraCheck: one noodle lifted on a fork
steps.videoShot: noodles lifted from the water with tongs

steps.title: Drain the noodles in the colander and rinse them under cold running water
steps.text: Drain the noodles in the colander and rinse them under cold running water
steps.tip: rinsing stops the cooking and washes off surface starch, so the noodles don't clump.
steps.visualCue: the noodles feel cool to touch; steam stops rising
steps.videoShot: cold water running over noodles in a strainer

steps.title: Shake off the water, drizzle ½ tsp oil over the noodles, toss gently and spread them on a plate
steps.text: Shake off the water, drizzle ½ tsp oil over the noodles, toss gently and spread them on a plate
steps.visualCue: glossy, separate strands that do not stick together
steps.cameraCheck: the oiled noodles spread on a plate
steps.videoShot: noodles tossed with oil using fingers or forks

steps.title: Heat the wok on high heat until very hot
steps.text: Heat the wok on high heat until very hot
steps.visualCue: a drop of water sizzles and vanishes in 1–2 seconds; faint smoke may rise
steps.videoShot: water flicked into the wok, evaporating instantly

steps.title: Add 2 tsp (10 g) oil and swirl it around the wok
steps.text: Add 2 tsp (10 g) oil and swirl it around the wok
steps.visualCue: the oil shimmers and flows thin
steps.videoShot: oil swirled up the sides of the wok

steps.title: Add the garlic, ginger and green chilli, and stir-fry
steps.text: Add the garlic, ginger and green chilli, and stir-fry
steps.tip: if the garlic browns fast, pull the wok off the flame for a few seconds. Burnt garlic tastes bitter.
steps.visualCue: strong garlic smell; garlic just turns pale gold at the edges
steps.videoShot: garlic sizzling in the oil

steps.title: Add the sliced onion and the spring onion whites, and stir-fry
steps.text: Add the sliced onion and the spring onion whites, and stir-fry
steps.visualCue: onion turns glossy and slightly translucent but still crunchy
steps.videoShot: onion tossed with the spatula

steps.title: Add the carrot and beans, and stir-fry on high heat
steps.text: Add the carrot and beans, and stir-fry on high heat
steps.visualCue: brighter colour; carrot still crunchy when pressed
steps.cameraCheck: the carrots and beans in the wok
steps.videoShot: vegetables tossed in the wok

steps.title: Add the cabbage and capsicum, and stir-fry
steps.text: Add the cabbage and capsicum, and stir-fry
steps.tip: keep the flame high and keep the vegetables moving. They should still crunch.
steps.visualCue: cabbage wilts slightly at the edges; everything is bright and crisp-tender
steps.videoShot: green vegetables added and tossed

steps.title: Add the boiled noodles to the wok
steps.text: Add the boiled noodles to the wok
steps.visualCue: noodles resting on top of the vegetables
steps.videoShot: noodles dropped into the wok

steps.title: Pour the sauce mix over the noodles and sprinkle the pepper, salt and sugar
steps.text: Pour the sauce mix over the noodles and sprinkle the pepper, salt and sugar
steps.visualCue: a loud sizzle and a savoury, slightly smoky smell
steps.cameraCheck: the sauce going into the wok
steps.videoShot: sauce drizzled over the noodles, sizzling

steps.title: Toss the noodles with tongs or two forks, lifting from the bottom, on high heat
steps.text: Toss the noodles with tongs or two forks, lifting from the bottom, on high heat
steps.tip: lift and drop instead of stirring. Stirring with a spatula breaks the noodles. Taste a strand before adding any more salt.
steps.visualCue: noodles evenly light brown with no pale patches; vegetables spread through them; noodles hot right through
steps.cameraCheck: evenly coloured noodles in the wok
steps.videoShot: noodles lifted high with tongs and dropped back

steps.title: Add the spring onion greens, toss for 15 seconds, and turn off the flame
steps.text: Add the spring onion greens, toss for 15 seconds, and turn off the flame
steps.visualCue: bright green flecks throughout
steps.cameraCheck: the finished noodles in the wok
steps.videoShot: spring onion scattered and tossed in

steps.text: Transfer to a plate or bowl and serve immediately

reasons: the home version uses 2½ tsp oil, about 180 g of vegetables (as much vegetable as cooked noodle) and moderate sauce. It is still built on refined maida noodles with about 12 g protein, and the sauces push sodium to about 1 g. Restaurant and street versions typically use 2–3 tbsp oil, often add MSG (ajinomoto), use more soy and chilli sauce, and have a much higher noodle-to-vegetable ratio, so sodium and calories are higher and fibre is lower.

researchRating.basis: veg hakka noodles are one of the most-ordered Indo-Chinese dishes in India and a Mumbai street-food staple. The top recipe pages are rated close to perfect (Indian Healthy Recipes 4.99/5 from 155 votes; Tarla Dalal's Mumbai roadside version 5/5 and vegetable hakka noodles 4.9/5 from 12 reviews). It loses a little because many home cooks say their noodles turn sticky or bland compared with the street version, and a few recipes score lower (Whisk Affair 4.1/5 from 10 votes).

storage: Fridge: cool within 1 hour and keep in an airtight container for up to 1 day (at most 2). The noodles soften and soak up the sauce. Freezer: not recommended; the noodles turn mushy and the vegetables go limp when thawed. Reheating: toss in a hot pan with 1 tsp oil and a splash of water for 2 minutes until steaming hot, or microwave covered with a sprinkle of water for 1–1.5 min, stirring halfway. Reheat only once.
leftoverRemix: make crispy noodle cutlets. Chop about 1 cup leftover noodles, mix with 1 small mashed boiled potato, 1 tbsp cornflour and a pinch of chilli flakes, shape into flat patties, and shallow-fry or air-fry until crisp on both sides. Serve with Schezwan chutney or ketchup.
burnOff: Running: about 6.5 km at about 70 kcal per km. Walking: about 9 km at a brisk pace (est.), using about 50 kcal per km.
